description: Port 64444 services the multiplexing of port addresses for ports beyond the standard 2^16 (65536) range, extending addressable port space to 30 quintillion (30,000,000,000,000,000,000).

extended_port_range.note: Ports 0-65535 remain directly addressable via standard TCP/UDP headers. Ports above 65535 require multiplexing through port 64444.

trigger.description: Send a single ASCII character '1' or the string '1s' to port 64444 to receive this protocol specification.

discovery.response: This entire JSON document is returned upon receiving '1' or '1s'.

phase_1_key_exchange.description: Initial key exchange uses Diffie-Hellman to establish a shared secret. This shared secret is used to encrypt the subsequent RSA public key exchange.

steps.action: Client sends DH public value (g^a mod p)
Server sends DH public value (g^b mod p)
Both parties compute shared secret (g^ab mod p)
steps.derived_key: AES-256 key derived via HKDF-SHA256 from shared secret

phase_2_rsa_exchange.description: After DH key exchange, RSA public keys are exchanged encrypted under the DH-derived AES key. All subsequent communication uses RSA encryption.

steps.action: Client sends RSA public key, encrypted with DH-derived AES-256 key
Server sends RSA public key, encrypted with DH-derived AES-256 key
Server sends session confirmation signed with server RSA private key

phase_3_data_mode_negotiation.description: Client declares whether subsequent data will be sent as raw (unencrypted) or encrypted (RSA-encrypted). This selection applies to the payload of extended port data frames.

raw.description: Client will send raw/plaintext data. Server trusts the DH+RSA handshake authenticated the client. No per-message encryption applied to payloads.
raw.use_case: High-throughput scenarios where authentication is sufficient and confidentiality is handled at another layer (e.g., VPN, physical security).

encrypted.description: Client will send RSA-encrypted data for each message. Each payload is encrypted with the server's RSA public key.
encrypted.use_case: Standard secure communication where per-message confidentiality is required.

hybrid.description: Client will send AES-256-GCM encrypted data using a session key derived from the RSA exchange. RSA encrypts only the session key.
hybrid.use_case: Balanced performance and security for large payloads.

steps.action: Server acknowledges data mode and confirms session is ready

extended_port_frame.description: After handshake completes, the client sends frames through port 64444 that are demultiplexed to the target extended port.

target_port.description: The extended port number (0 to 30,000,000,000,000,000,000) to route this frame to

source_port.description: The client's extended source port for return routing

payload_length.description: Length of the payload in bytes

sequence.description: Frame sequence number for ordering and reassembly

extended_port_frame.note: Frames larger than max_payload_bytes must be fragmented using the fragmented/final_fragment flags.

error_codes.0x01: INVALID_PORT - Target port out of range
error_codes.0x02: PORT_UNREACHABLE - No service listening on target extended port
error_codes.0x03: HANDSHAKE_FAILED - Key exchange did not complete
error_codes.0x07: MODE_MISMATCH - Payload encryption does not match negotiated mode

security_considerations: Port 64444 MUST be protected by host firewall (UFW/iptables/nftables) rules.
DH parameters MUST be at least 2048 bits; 4096 bits recommended.
RSA keys MUST be at least 2048 bits; 4096 bits recommended.
Session timeout: 3600 seconds (1 hour) of inactivity triggers re-handshake.
Failed handshake attempts rate-limited to 5 per minute per source IP.
Raw data mode should only be used within trusted network segments.

firewall_integration.nftables_example: nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 64444 accept
